**Finding: Missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

The Agreement locks us in for three years (§ 8.1) with a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1), while § 9 contains only cause-based exits (breach, insolvency, security/service-level/legal/IP failures). There is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere — a deviation under the playbook for any term longer than 12 months. Notably, Vendor also has no convenience right, so only the Customer-side gap needs fixing.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):**
- New § 9.4: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, with a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, proportionate reduction of minimum commitments, and no early-termination penalty; Vendor gets no convenience right during a committed term.
- § 2.1 conformed so the take-or-pay language is "subject to Customer's reduction and termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4" — otherwise the new right would be neutered.

Fallback offered in the comment if Vendor pushes back: 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.
